gen-dafont-junegull-gf-hedvig-letters-se: Hedvig Letters Serif reads like a classic serif with sturdy, lofty lowercase and curves left open to breathe. And Junegull does the opposite job, pinching its curves shut and giving every letter a flat, cast-iron presence.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-marcellus-sc: Marcellus SC reads dignified and literary, its stems barely heavier than the arms they connect to and its terminals pulled well back. Junegull is the blunter one, pinched and uniform.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-montagu-slab: Wire-bent from end to end, Junegull gives each word a pinched, retro look with no thick-thin flicker anywhere. And Montagu Slab brings robust downstrokes, slender turns and an open e, so the pair's real strength is how firmly they differ.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-ovo: Authoritative and classic, Ovo varies its strokes softly, with thins just a touch lighter than its thicks. But Junegull keeps one skimming line throughout, so the display heading and the serif body move at different speeds.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-hanuman: Wide, loose and round, like a rolling-ball pen. Hanuman holds the opposite corner, a refined serif with a high-waisted lowercase, and that gap between playful and traditional is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-kadwa: Kadwa reads classic and editorial, a serif with open-ended curves and a lowercase that stands larger than usual. And Lemon Milk does its best work up top, spread wide in rounded letters with no hairline anywhere.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla reads refined and authoritative, its lowercase running close to the capitals and its e opened like a pried clasp. Lemon Milk goes loose, wide and rounded.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-pridi: Lemon Milk sprawls wide and loose, friendly and striking. It handles the bold rounded work at the top, and Pridi, a classic serif with generous gaps and proud small letters, handles the steadier reading below.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-suwannaphum: Suwannaphum reads dignified and editorial, with a c as open as a bent paperclip and a lowercase standing high like squared-off woodblock type. And over many lines Lemon Milk's rounded, zero-contrast letters give way to that serif's livelier, more varied strokes.
gen-dafont-nasalization-gf-domine: Domine reads refined, with compact ascenders and room inside every curve. Nasalization floats its big lowercase letters well apart, and that friendly looseness against a dignified serif is the pair's strongest quality.
